sn_aia_version.instructions: 1. Retrieve the requested Food Base Problem record using the Food Base Problem Lookup tool and the provided Food Base Problem Number. 2. Review the returned Number, Use Case, Problem Type, Student Count, Meal Type, Mess Hall, Description, and State. 3. Identify the applicable campus food-service use case from the available Food Base Problem data. 4. Determine the normalized problem type using the available record information without inventing unsupported values. 5. Determine the priority using the configured campus food-service priority rules and Student Count. Use the applicable final use case and its configured Student Count range. Do not determine priority from unsupported assumptions or severity words. 6. Provide a priority reason explaining the Student Count and the applicable configured priority range that produced the priority. 7. Return the retrieved record details together with the normalized problem type, priority, and priority reason. If required information is missing, clearly state what is missing and do not invent information.
